title: Local LM Studio Evaluation
text: This walkthrough documents the local smoke test in xp/lmstudio_eval.py. It connects a local LM Studio inference server (http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1) with the ScreamingFace evaluation runtime on medxpert. The script defaults to one question and the solo candidate only; it is a connectivity check, not an accuracy comparison. For the broader research scripts, see the experiment guide.

title: Local LM Studio Evaluation
text:
2 Environment & Server Setup
Sync the project environment with uv sync --extra dev. Start the LM Studio server with a model loaded, then prepare the benchmark and start ScreamingFace with its local-model overlay enabled:
uv run screamingface prepare medxpert
AIGW_LOCAL_ENABLED=true uv run screamingface up
If the stack is already running, use AIGW_LOCAL_ENABLED=true uv run screamingface restart to apply the changed Gateway setting. Set the SDK’s Engine and Scoreboard endpoints in the shell used for evaluation:
export SCREAMINGFACE_ENGINE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9108
export SCREAMINGFACE_SCOREBOARD_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9106

title: Local LM Studio Evaluation
text:
3 Model Discovery & Selection
The script discovers local models exposed through the ScreamingFace overlay (local/* prefix) and automatically picks the target model using fuzzy matching:
#| eval: false
import screamingface as sf
import screamingface._environment
from tk.r.openmined import common as clib

screamingface._environment.ipykernel_loaded = lambda: False
if hasattr(sf.report.Report, "_ipython_display_"):
    del sf.report.Report._ipython_display_

print(f"screamingface {sf.__version__} ready.")

# Discover models mirrored from LM Studio (http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/models)
local_models = [m.id for m in sf.models.list() if m.id.startswith("local/")]
assert local_models, "expect lmstudio + ScreamingFace w/ AIGW_LOCAL_ENABLED=true."

ACTIVE_MODEL = "local/google/gemma-4-e4b"
closest = clib.closestname(ACTIVE_MODEL, local_models)
ACTIVE_MODEL = closest[0]
print(f"Using active model: {ACTIVE_MODEL}")

title: Local LM Studio Evaluation
text:
4 Candidate Architectures
We define two candidate approaches to compare single-model generation against multi-pass refinement:

4.1 Recipe 1: Solo Local Model
Direct generation using the selected local model:
#| eval: false
solo = sf.Model(ACTIVE_MODEL, name="solo-local")


4.2 Recipe 2: Two-Pass Self-Refinement Chain
A pipeline where the first pass drafts an initial answer, and a second pass reviews and verifies it:
#| eval: false
chain = sf.Pipeline(
    [
        sf.Model(ACTIVE_MODEL, name="draft"),
        sf.Model(
            ACTIVE_MODEL,
            prompt="Review and verify this medical answer:\n\n{context}\n\nFinal answer:",
        ),
    ],
    name="local-refine-chain",
)

title: Local LM Studio Evaluation
text:
5 Benchmark Execution
Evaluations are triggered via sf.evaluate:
#| eval: false
BENCHMARK = "medxpert"
LIMIT = 1

candidates = [solo]  # Add `chain` to benchmark multi-pass refinement

print(f"Running evaluation on {BENCHMARK=} (limit={LIMIT})...")
report = sf.evaluate(candidates, benchmark=BENCHMARK, limit=LIMIT)

title: Local LM Studio Evaluation
text:
6 Results & Output Inspection
The benchmark outputs candidate scores, costs, and individual test cases:
#| eval: false
print("\n" + "=" * 60)
print(f"{'Candidate':<30} | {'Score':^10} | {'Cost':^12}")
print("-" * 60)
for c in report.candidates:
    score = f"{c.score:.3f}" if c.score is not None else "N/A"
    cost = "$0.00 (local)"
    print(f"{c.name:<30} | {score:^10} | {cost:^12}")
print("=" * 60)

for candidate in report.candidates:
    print(f"\nOutputs for {candidate.name}:")
    for case in candidate.cases:
        score = case.grade.score if case.grade else 0.0
        status = "PASS" if score and score > 0 else "FAIL"
        clean_output = (case.output or "").strip().replace("\n", " ")[:120]
        print(f"  [Case {case.case_id}] {status} (score={score}): {clean_output}...")

6.1 Sample Output
Illustrative one-question output from the original walkthrough, not a current benchmark result or a measured accuracy estimate. The script’s $0.00 (local) label is hardcoded; it does not account for local hardware or energy costs.
============================================================
Candidate                      |   Score    |     Cost
------------------------------------------------------------
solo-local                     |   0.000    | $0.00 (local)
============================================================

Outputs for solo-local:
  [Case 1] FAIL (score=0.0): The correct answer is **(H)**...

title: Local LM Studio Evaluation
text:
7 Reproducing Locally
Run the smoke test directly with uv. The active model name, benchmark, limit, and candidate list are configured in the script rather than through CLI flags:
uv run python xp/lmstudio_eval.py
All code blocks on this page are display-only. To re-render the site without running the evaluation:
quarto render docs

title: Ensembles and Routing
text:
For a given cost or latency, what’s the best accuracy anyone can reach — and which method and combination of models gets there?

This repository explores single-model baselines, repeated-sample voting, Mixture-of-Agents, confidence-based cascades, and learned routing using ScreamingFace.
The current scripts primarily compare accuracy and per-question generation cost. They do not yet establish a latency frontier. Collection runs evaluate candidates through ScreamingFace; several routing and cascade studies then replay decisions over saved answers rather than executing a live adaptive policy.

title: Ensembles and Routing
text:
Status and evidence
The experiment scripts are implementations and prototypes, not a published results report. No experiment CSVs are present in this checkout’s results/ or xp/results/ directories. Those directories are ignored by Git, so their absence does not establish whether experiments ran elsewhere.
The LM Studio walkthrough includes illustrative output from a one-question smoke test, not an accuracy estimate. P6 still needs a verified image benchmark; P7 separates external token-logprob research from its ScreamingFace verbalized-confidence proxy. See the experiment guide for these limitations.

title: Ensembles and Routing
text:
Updating this site
Edit the .qmd source pages and docs/_quarto.yml, then run from the repository root:
quarto render docs
For an interactive preview:
quarto preview docs
Quarto is installed separately from the Python project. The site renders into docs/ itself (output-dir: .), not docs/_site/. Generated HTML, search metadata, and site_libs/ are tracked alongside the sources; include their changes when publishing a documentation update. Do not edit the generated HTML directly.
Code examples are display-only Markdown fences, so rendering this site does not run experiments, require an inference server, or make model API calls.

title: Experiment Guide
text:
The numbered studies are independent collectors, not a pipeline that must be run in order. Source links below point to the repository; new local scripts must also be committed before those links are available on GitHub.



Study
Source
Implemented comparison
Important qualification




P1: MoA vs Self-MoA
2610_moa_vs_selfmoa.py
Solo models, repeated-sample voting, and mixed-model voting; optional single- and two-layer synthesis.
Default runs voting baselines only. Add --fusion for MoA/Self-MoA; --no-layered skips two-layer MoA. “Best” is the configured frontier model, and “equal-spend” pairs are nearest-cost comparisons, not strictly matched budgets.


P2: cascade signals
2610_cascade_signals.py
Stage solos, confidence-prompt controls, cheap voting, then offline confidence/agreement cascades and optional frozen routers.
Routing is replayed over cached answers. Signals are verbalized confidence, self-agreement, and cross-model agreement, not token logprobs. Thresholds use a dev split, but the accuracy target uses held-out frontier accuracy.


P3: voting curves
p3_voting_curves.py
Seeded samples, simulated plurality curves, difficulty slices, adaptive stopping, and live votes at N=3 and N=9.
Reports tables, not a plot. Resampling bands reflect available seeds rather than question-level uncertainty. Model support for seeded sampling must be checked.


P4: RouteLLM transfer
p4_routellm_transfer.py
Strong/weak solos with frozen-router threshold sweeps, APGR, and an oracle comparison.
Offline replay; consumes its own strong/weak candidates, not P2’s stage-named outputs.


P5: kNN routing robustness
p5_knn_routing_robustness.py
Multi-model, multi-benchmark collection, kNN routing, leave-one-benchmark-out transfer, and paraphrase stability.
Multiple benchmarks are needed for out-of-domain analysis. The in-domain split pools benchmark-qualified question IDs; paraphrase stability includes training and test IDs.


P6: multimodal routing
p6_multimodal_routing.py
Vision solos, voting, describe-then-reason, and offline routing by image type.
Prototype: inspect-mmmu is a placeholder, not a verified available benchmark. A real image benchmark and image-capable routes are prerequisites.


P7: confidence-filtered voting
p7_confidence_filtered_vote.py
External token-logprob collection and DeepConf-style analysis; separate ScreamingFace verbalized-confidence proxy.
The proxy is not token-logprob DeepConf. External collection is research-only, not a ScreamingFace leaderboard result.

title: Experiment Guide
text:
Environment and runtime
Run commands from the repository root so exports land in the expected results/ directory. Install the project dependencies first:
uv sync --extra dev
Python must satisfy the range in pyproject.toml (currently >=3.12,<3.15). Model routes, token limits, and cost assumptions live in src/tk/r/openmined/common.py. Confirm that your Engine serves the selected routes and benchmark before a live run; the scripts check these before evaluation.
For the normal local runtime, prepare the intended benchmark and start the stack. For example, P1’s default benchmark can be prepared with:
uv run python -m screamingface_engine.benchmarks.prepare \
  --root ~/.screamingface/benchmark-assets \
  --bundle inspect-lab_bench_litqa
uv run screamingface up
If the stack is already running, use uv run screamingface restart to apply changed Gateway settings. The normal launcher supplies the prepared benchmark assets to the Engine. Set the SDK endpoints in the shell used for experiments:
export SCREAMINGFACE_ENGINE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9108
export SCREAMINGFACE_SCOREBOARD_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9106
Remote routes need a connected provider and valid credentials. Live runs send benchmark prompts to the selected providers and can incur charges. Keep API keys out of source files and published reports. Prepared benchmarks, served routes, free-model availability, and provider parameter support can change independently of these scripts.
P1 and P2 support --free, but the normal Engine does not necessarily declare both free routes. The custom configuration is xp/gemma-free.toml; the setup notes at the top of xp/tktest.py describe a separate Engine on port 9109. Gateway model IDs use :free, while Engine route IDs use ~free. Do not run tktest.py as a setup command: its top-level code makes network calls and evaluates a model.

title: Experiment Guide
text:
Inspect a plan without evaluating
These commands take the dry-run branches, which do not contact the Engine or run inference. Cost estimates are rough planning aids, not spend caps. Dry-run success does not verify that a route or benchmark exists.
uv run python xp/2610_moa_vs_selfmoa.py --benchmark inspect-lab_bench_litqa --limit 5 --k 3 --fusion --dry-run
uv run python xp/2610_cascade_signals.py --benchmark inspect-mmlu_pro --limit 5 --dry-run
uv run python xp/p3_voting_curves.py --benchmark inspect-mmlu_pro --limit 5 --tiers cheap frontier --dry-run
uv run python xp/p4_routellm_transfer.py --benchmark inspect-mmlu_pro --limit 5 --routers bert random --dry-run
uv run python xp/p5_knn_routing_robustness.py --limit 5 --paraphrase-limit 5 --dry-run
uv run python xp/p6_multimodal_routing.py --dry-run
uv run python xp/p7_confidence_filtered_vote.py proxy --benchmark inspect-aime25 --n 8 --threshold 0.6 --dry-run
P6 remains a plan preview until its benchmark and routes are verified. P7’s proxy has no --limit option; removing its --dry-run can evaluate the full benchmark. The parsers use parse_known_args(), so an unsupported option may be silently ignored rather than rejected.

title: Experiment Guide
text:
Collect and analyze
After checking the plan and runtime, explicitly remove --dry-run to collect. For example, a small P1 run with synthesis enabled is:
uv run python xp/2610_moa_vs_selfmoa.py --benchmark inspect-lab_bench_litqa --limit 5 --k 3 --fusion
Shared collection exports both a full report and per-case rows:

results/<tag>.report.json: the ScreamingFace report.
results/<tag>.csv: candidate, case ID, score, generation cost, output, input, and abstention status.

Tags start with p1_ through p6_, or p7_proxy_, and include the benchmark. These filenames are deterministic: repeating a run with the same tag overwrites its exports. Archive artifacts before rerunning a configuration you want to retain. Partially failed evaluations preserve the candidates that completed when ScreamingFace returns a partial report; a saved file alone does not establish a complete comparison.
P1–P6 support --analyze for their own saved CSVs. Quote globs so the script expands them, and keep input files benchmark-specific unless intentionally doing P5’s cross-benchmark analysis:
uv run python xp/2610_moa_vs_selfmoa.py --analyze "results/p1_inspect-lab_bench_litqa*.csv"
uv run python xp/2610_cascade_signals.py --benchmark inspect-mmlu_pro --analyze "results/p2_inspect-mmlu_pro*.csv" --routers bert random
uv run python xp/p4_routellm_transfer.py --benchmark inspect-mmlu_pro --analyze "results/p4_inspect-mmlu_pro*.csv" --routers bert random
uv run python xp/p5_knn_routing_robustness.py --analyze "results/p5_*.csv"
Preserve relevant collection options such as --numeric and --models when analyzing. Router analysis may download checkpoints, and P5 may download sentence-transformer weights. RouteLLM’s mf router additionally needs OPENAI_API_KEY for embeddings; cached-answer analysis is not necessarily network-free.

Cost interpretation
The shared exporter excludes grading from generation cost and keeps unknown costs as unknown. For configured routes, a zero-dollar call with known token usage (such as a free route or cache hit) is repriced using PRICES to estimate cold-call cost. Consequently, plotted cost is not necessarily the amount billed. See common.py for the current rates and extraction rules.
The scripts do not provide a complete end-to-end latency accounting protocol. Do not interpret offline cost curves as measured serving latency.

title: Experiment Guide
text:
P7 token-logprob research
P7’s collect subcommand bypasses ScreamingFace and calls an OpenAI-compatible endpoint directly. It requires:

A problems JSONL file with id and prompt fields.
A gold-answer JSON object mapping IDs to answers.
OPENROUTER_API_KEY, which the current implementation reads even when --base-url is supplied.
A provider/model combination that actually returns token logprobs.

Collection appends to results/p7_traces.jsonl by default, so repeating it can duplicate samples. Once valid traces exist, analyze them with:
uv run python xp/p7_confidence_filtered_vote.py analyze --traces results/p7_traces.jsonl --window 2048
This external analysis and the verbalized-confidence proxy answer different questions; report them separately. Synthetic assertions embedded in the scripts are implementation checks, not empirical benchmark findings.
